verdict.summary: A configuration change at 11:59:19 set shippingservice's QUOTE_SERVICE_ADDR to a non-existent quote host, so GetQuote calls could no longer be fulfilled and the failure surfaced as errors in checkoutservice's PlaceOrder path.
verdict.reasoning: checkoutservice error ratio departed from baseline at 12:00:15 (tr_800ba88abbf8), but every failing trace fails at the same hop: checkout's client span to ShippingService/GetQuote is the error-marked, dominant segment, while the rest of checkout's fan-out (cart, catalog, currency) is fast and clean (tr_463ac633c5ad). checkoutservice itself had no changes in the preceding 24h (tr_cbe3ab7aba02), which rules out its own artifact or settings. shippingservice, by contrast, had an environment edit applied at 11:59:19 repointing its quote-service address to a host that does not exist (tr_a0dde5982de3), about a minute before onset; the same edit-and-revert pair had been exercised twice earlier in the day. shippingservice's own log stream shows quote requests still arriving after that time without the completed-quote follow-ups that accompanied them earlier in the window (tr_a64fa48250b8), consistent with the outbound quote lookup no longer resolving. The wrongness of the address value is itself the failure, so this is bad_config rather than a deploy or exhaustion; checkoutservice and loadgenerator alerted because the error propagates toward the caller.
open_questions: The elided middle of the shipping log window means I did not directly observe connection-failure lines between 11:32 and 12:00, only the absence of quote completions in the newest lines.
Whether the 11:59 change has since been reverted (no revert record appears yet), and whether any traffic still succeeded.
Why shippingservice's server span is not itself error-marked while checkout's client span is - the error may be carried in the gRPC status rather than the span flag.
